about: The API audit (scripts/contracts/api.mjs): every option, event, and string choice of the spec reaches each surface under the name that surface's convention makes of it. The spec, TypeScript, and the adapters spell options in camelCase, Python in snake_case; React's listeners are onSelect, Svelte's onselect, Vue's events select, and the notebook widget's on_select; a handle's getter and setter are the widget's property of their name (getHiddenKeys and setHiddenKeys, hidden_keys), where api.json spells them otherwise (the widget's get_viewport and set_viewport are methods); Python's mark methods split a number from its word (point_3d); and a Vue template's bare attribute (`<Line dodge />`) is true for every option of a mark component that takes true.

Each audit's differences from its convention, with the reason: spelled (a reference option the surface spells otherwise), spread (a reference option whose settings are the surface's own options, each spelled by the convention after prefix, or as `as` says), without (a reference option the surface does not take), only (an option of the surface's own), choices (an option whose string choices differ: `takes`, the surface's, which it must take), and untyped (settings one side types and the other takes untyped). `<audit> <option>` audits the settings of an option both sides type, at any depth (`chart python x`: the spec's x axis and hg.AxisOptions). `mark * <surface>` and `mark * <surface> <option>` list what every mark's audit of that surface shares, and `express * ...` what every Express function's does. `express <function> seaborn` compares an Express function with seaborn's of the same name.

The surfaces' behavior is proved by the spec contracts (packages/herceg/test/fixtures/contracts.json), whose cases each surface makes and draws; the audit proves the names and choices they are made with.
Documented defaults are proved alike in the spec and in Python by test/contracts/fixtures/defaults.json's cases (`<contract>.spec`, `<contract>.python`).

only.inset: Draws a panel over this panel's plot.
only.legend: The panel's own legend, which a chart places with its legend option.

without.legend: A helper's legend is its chart's (HelperOptions), whose one mark is its series.
without.facet: A helper's facet is its chart's (HelperOptions): its small multiples.
without.tooltip: A helper's tooltip is its chart's (HelperOptions).
without.width: A helper's width is its chart's (HelperOptions); bars take theirs from Chart.bar.

only.fill: Python's one hg.Encodings serves every mark; a mark refuses the channels it has not (`line encode: has no fill channel; give "color", "stroke", ...`).

only.marker: Python's one hg.MarkStyle serves every mark; a mark refuses what it does not take (`area style: has no marker; give "by"`).

span.reason: Python takes a bare value as a data position (hg.DataPosition), where the spec writes {data: value}.

from.reason: from is a Python keyword; PEP 8 adds the underscore.

bands.reason: Python takes each band as its end, or its end and color, (to, color), where the spec writes {to, color}.

untyped.bands: Python takes each band as its end, or its end and color, (to, color), where the spec writes { to, color }.

only.geojson: Plotly's way to give shapes, as Python users bring them: a GeoJSON object, which Python makes the spec's shapes table.
only.locations: With geojson, the rows' column of feature ids, which Python joins to the shapes.
only.feature_id_key: With geojson, the feature property the ids are read from.

px.reason: Python's hg.Pixels takes its number as value (`{ px: 4 }` is `hg.Pixels(4)`).

only.field: Python's hg.Pixels serves places too; a bar's width refuses a place's settings (`bar width: a length is pixels alone; drop field, frame, and offset`).

without.condition: Python writes a condition as hg.when(condition, then, otherwise) in the channel's place, not as a setting of hg.Channel. TypeScript writes the spec's { condition: { when, then, otherwise } }, whose then key linters flag (Biome's noThenProperty); a spec holds no functions, so no condition is a thenable, and the spec keeps one form until channels take per-row expressions in every language.
